subject: E-Commerce
title: Amazon Aggregators: Roll-Up and Burn Out
description: A fast breakdown of Amazon Aggregators: Roll-Up and Burn Out for builders.

hook.text: Amazon aggregators raised $16 billion to buy top sellers. Then most of them collapsed. Thrasio filed for bankruptcy.

buildup.text: Aggregators like Thrasio, Perch, and Heyday bought profitable Amazon brands, planning to optimize and scale them.

discovery.text: The thesis: buying 50 brands, centralizing operations, and cross-selling would create Amazon mega-empires.

twist.text: Rising Amazon fees, increased competition, and ad costs crushed margins. Brands looked profitable weren't after scaling.

climax.text: $16 billion burned on a thesis that Amazon sells you success but controls the cost of keeping it.

punchline.text: $16B raised, Thrasio bankrupt. Buying Amazon businesses proved you can't own.

quiz.question: Why did most Amazon aggregators fail?
options: Rising Amazon fees and ad costs destroyed the margins they assumed would stay stable
